question.prompt: Tell me about a time you failed or made a mistake on a project. What happened, and what did you learn from the experience?
expectedPoints: Authentic admission of a personal mistake or misjudgment
Immediate containment and remediation actions taken
Root cause analysis avoiding deflection of blame onto others
Concrete lasting improvements to process, tooling, or personal habits
commonMistakes: Giving a fake failure ("I worked too hard")
Blaming managers, stakeholders, or junior devs exclusively
Failing to share genuine post-incident learnings

transcript: Candidate: Honestly, I don't really have major failures because I am very meticulous with my work. But one time a project was delivered two months late. That wasn't really my failure though—our product manager kept changing the specifications every week, and upper management cut our team budget in half. If management had given us clear requirements from day one, we would have shipped early. What did I learn? I learned that management rarely knows what they are doing and that you can't trust timelines when other people are involved.
notes: Refuses to acknowledge personal vulnerability, blames management, cynical takeaway.
